Reuters reports that Russia's antitrust regulator has formally launched an investigation into Apple for failing to preinstall the state-backed messaging app MAX and the Russian app store RuStore on its devices. Below is the detailed coverage.

Russia files antitrust lawsuit against Apple

Since 2019, when Russia passed a law requiring device manufacturers to offer domestic apps on products sold locally, Apple has been locked in a protracted tug-of-war with Russian authorities.

When the law came into effect in 2021, Apple reached an arrangement with the authorities whereby Russian users setting up a new iPhone would be shown a list of recommended Russian-developed apps, rather than having them preinstalled automatically.

In March 2022, following Russia's invasion of Ukraine, Apple stopped selling and exporting products in the country, and removed the RT News and Sputnik News apps from the App Store outside Russia. In September of the same year, Apple also removed several apps belonging to Russian tech company VK, citing UK sanctions.

Last year, Russia began requiring that all new smartphones and tablets sold locally come preinstalled with the state-backed messaging app MAX, while extending the mandate to preinstall the RuStore app store to Apple devices. Apple has not complied with either requirement.

Tensions escalated further in June, when Apple removed MAX from the Russian App Store, followed later that month by the removal of several more apps developed by VK. Apple said the removals were necessary to comply with sanctions.

This prompted Russia's Federal Antimonopoly Service to order the company to address what it called discriminatory treatment of domestic software by July 15. Apple reportedly partially complied, allowing the preinstallation of a Russian search engine in iOS 26.6, but has still not implemented the requirements related to MAX and RuStore.

According to Reuters, after Apple failed to fully comply with the warning, Russia has now formally launched an antitrust investigation into Apple.

Original report:

It remains unclear what penalties the company could face if Russia finds it has violated its competition laws. In 2024, Russia had calculated accumulated fines of around $20 decillion (a 2 followed by 33 zeros) against Google for its years-long refusal to restore banned Russian state and pro-Kremlin channels on YouTube.

Apple has not yet responded to the investigation.
